about: Shared smart progression contract. Edit this file, then run `node scripts/sync_progression_fixtures.cjs` to copy it into both apps. Android ProgressionFixturesTest and iOS ProgressionFixtureTests execute every case. Loads are written in `unit` (or a log's `loadUnit`) and converted with each app's canonical kilogram conversion. Expected targets use the case `unit` unless `targetUnit` says otherwise. Formatting cases give the rounded `display` label, the lossless two-decimal `exact` text, and the text a set or target receives for other lifts (`loadable`) and barbell lifts (`barbell`). A load that reads back on the two-decimal grid in `unit` stays exact. A converted barbell load takes the multiple of 5 lb / 2.5 kg within 2.5% that needs the fewest standard plates per side on a 45 lb / 20 kg bar (lb: 45, 35, 25, 10, 5, 2.5; kg: 25, 20, 15, 10, 5, 2.5, 1.25), ties going to the closer, then lighter, load; other converted loads round to the nearest 5 lb or 2.5 kg. A positive load never rounds to zero and keeps one decimal instead. `applied` is the input text Apply Target (or Use lighter week) writes; Apply must also store the target's canonical kilograms unchanged, leave reps empty and show the target reps as their placeholder. A case `context` is the active workout day and current time, as the session screen passes them; records default to programId and workoutId `fixture`, and `snapshot` lists the prescription saved with a record. `steps` sets the dumbbell/machine load-step settings in the case unit (defaults: 2 kg / 5 kg, 5 lb / 10 lb); `platesKg` and `platesLbs` set each unit's available plates (defaults include 1.25 kg and 2.5 lb); `barType` is the Warmup & Plates bar key (default `olympic_20`: 20 kg / 45 lb), where a bar step's grid starts. A log's `effort` is easy, right or hard. `variation` is the suggested exercise ID; `rationaleArgs` lists arguments that must match. A log's optional `techniques` list adds a drop, rest-pause or partials to its working set at 1-based position `set`: `technique` (`drop` or `restPause`) with `extensions` as [load, reps] pairs, and/or `partialReps`. `techniqueSets`, when given, lists the set numbers the card shows on its "Last time" line. A log's `rir` lists each working set's reps in reserve (0–4, 4 meaning 4+, or null for an unrated set). `adjustment` cases are the mid-workout load adjustment (adaptive-training.md, B2): `sets` are the exercise's current rows in order, where `load` and `reps` are typed values (a row without `load` is untouched), `done` marks a ticked set, `warmup` a warmup row and `rir` the set's reps in reserve. `expected` is null when nothing is offered; otherwise `direction` is easier or harder, `target` the load and rep goal in `unit`, `rows` the row indices Use fills and `applied` the load text each of those rows receives. After Use, nothing is offered again. `blockTarget` is a training block week's reps-in-reserve target (training-blocks.md), whose window replaces the default 1–3. A record's `blockId` marks a training-block session (training-blocks.md): its padded earlier-plan baseline confirms a load increase like a full session.
